newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Foreigners wounded in Ethiopia blast return home.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners wounded in Ethiopia blast return home.

text.p: Two British women, a French woman and a German man wounded in a grenade attack on an Ethiopian hotel have returned home, a British diplomat said on Thursday.
He said a third British woman, who was critically wounded by the blast at a hotel in the ancient eastern city of Harar on Monday night, remained at the Black Lion hospital in the capital Addis Ababa.
He declined to identify the wounded tourists.
Police said on Tuesday two people were killed and nine wounded when an unidentified attacker threw a hand grenade into the tourist hotel.
There have been no claims of responsibility for the attack.

Ethiopian authorities last year blamed Moslem fundamentalist "terrorists" for a series of bomb attacks in the east and the capital and sent troops in August on a two-day incursion into western Somalia to destroy several bases and training camps.
The Somali Moslem fundamentalist al-Ittihad al-Islami (Islamic Union) movement said Ethiopian troops backed by tanks invaded western Somalia again last September and December to hit its bases.
